fix_commit.message: Do not allow an integer overflow to bypass a leaf-term bound check in the integrity-check function of FTS5. [bugs:/info/2026-06-27T18:47:28Z|Bug 2026-06-27T18:47:28Z]
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: Integer overflow in leaf-term bound check allows out-of-bounds read in FTS5 integrity check
findings.message: In `fts5IndexIntegrityCheckSegment`, the expression `iOff+nTerm` uses 32-bit signed integer arithmetic. Both `iOff` (an `int` tracking the offset within a leaf page) and `nTerm` (an `int` decoded from a varint in potentially corrupted FTS5 data via `fts5GetVarint32`) are 32-bit signed values. If a malformed FTS5 database page encodes a large `nTerm` value such that `iOff+nTerm` wraps around (signed integer overflow, which is UB in C), the resulting value can be negative. A negative sum compares as less than `pLeaf->szLeaf` (a positive `int`), causing the bounds check `if( iOff+nTerm>pLeaf->szLeaf )` to pass incorrectly. Execution then falls through to `fts5Memcmp(&pLeaf->p[iOff], zIdxTerm, MIN(nTerm, nIdxTerm))`, which reads up to `nTerm` bytes starting at `iOff` within the leaf buffer — potentially far beyond its allocated size, resulting in an out-of-bounds read.
findings.suggestion: Cast all operands to a 64-bit signed integer before performing the addition and comparison, so overflow cannot occur. The fix is: `if( (i64)iOff+(i64)nTerm>(i64)pLeaf->szLeaf )`

ground_truth.root_cause: The bound check was written using native `int` arithmetic without considering that the sum of two `int` values (`iOff` and `nTerm`) could overflow a 32-bit signed integer. Since `nTerm` is attacker-controlled (read from a database page varint), an adversary can supply a value large enough to cause signed integer wraparound, turning the guard expression negative and defeating the check.
